They inspire me, so to get together to train was frankly amazing 😍 We are more than our MS 🧡 #fitness #gym #MS #multiplesclerosis #msawareness #fatigue #nervepain

when you find out your tumour marker numbers have dropped significantly,  that your lungs are cancer free, that your liver lesions have  almost  all gone and that that chemo is working!  Yay!!!  My story...May 2010 age 44.primary BC in left breast. Single mastectomy, lymph nodes removal,followed by 6 months FEC and Taxol chemo.  Jan 2014 secondaries found in 6th left rib. had part rib resection ( bloody painful) , 3 weeks daily radiation to chest wall. Started daily LeteozoleOopherectomy by key hole surgery. Sept 2019, lesions appear in two more ribs and a bit of soft tissue between. Put on Palbociclib with monthly Fulvestrant jabs. Sept 2021 many lesions appear in my lungs and liver with one large liver lesion off 3.9cm.  Tumour markers left from 40 to 240put on trial drug  Xeloda /Alpelicib Jan 2022 drug didn't work, more lesions, tumour marker now 420Put on Capecitabine March 2022 Cape not working either. More lesions, tumour marker 520April 2022 start weekly chemoMay 2022 tumour marker HALVES to 230June 2022 halves again to 108July 2022 now at 73 and dropping  #chemotherapy #livingwithcancer #livinglifetothefullest #secondarybreastcancer #chemosucks #abraxane #coldcap #chemocoldcaps #cancerthriver  #chemotherapysideeffects  #neuropathy

Cervical Radiculopathy (CR) otherwise known as a Pinched cervical nerve   This condition is caused by a compressed cervical spine nerve root.  Symptoms of CR is Pain that radiates down the arm from the neck along the course of the nerve. You may also experience muscle weakness and impaired tendon flexors.  Most frequently caused by disc trauma / herniation and commonly affects younger people in the 3rd and 4th decade.  Disc degeneration increases with age and people in the 5th and 6th decades are affected.  People in the 7th decade of life are likely to  experience CR due to spinal narrowing as a result of cartilage changes.  Treatment of CR -  85% are said to resolve in 8-12 weeks.  Physical therapy consists of gentle ROM exercises, Acupuncture to treat trigger points and ease inflammation, cervical traction and neurodynamics .  When pain is reduced you can work on posture and muscle imbalances with progressive exercises. 📌📌Trigger Finger  🎯 “Trigger Finger" (stenosing tenosynovitis) is a condition where inflammation of the tendon sheaths that surround the tendons of the hand cause impaired movement of the tendons, leading to decreased movement of the fingers that are affected ⚖️ Initially, people may notice a painless clicking during movement of the affected finger, but this can progress to painful catching or popping as symptoms progress 🔒 In some cases the finger may become "locked" in a bent position, requiring the other hand to push the finger straight again 🧠 The exact cause of trigger finger isn't always certain, but some potential contributing factors include any activity requiring prolonged forceful finger flexion/bending (i.e. carrying shopping bags or a briefcase, prolonged writing, rock climbing, or the strenuous grasping of small tools) 🥊This condition is more likely to develop in people in their 40s and 50s, 6 times more likely to develop in women, and 4 times more likely in people with diabetes • Conditions causing connective tissue changes such as rheumatoid arthritis and gout are also associated with trigger finger ✅ Treatment may include activity modification (including splinting if needed), anti-inflammatory medication, tendon gliding exercises or corticosteroid injections. 🎥 Here I show a few tendon gliding exercises that may be helpful in improving symptoms and mobility: 1️⃣Duck (or "tabletop") ﻿﻿﻿2️⃣Hook ﻿﻿3️⃣Full Fist ﻿﻿4️⃣Finger Spread ﻿﻿5️⃣Thumb to Tip 🗣️ Aim to perform these 2 times or more per day, with 10-20 repetitions each #physiotherapy #nerveglide #triggerfinger #pain #rehab #strength #power #physio #nervepain #rehabilitation #fingerpain #handandwrist #fyp #birdysong

Sciatica or Piriformis symptoms becoming a pain? Try this simple exercise to relieve it!! This is a nice gentle technique to help free up sciatic nerve to help it get a bit ‘unstuck’ and help relieve some of the pain! Start nice and gently and slowly try and get your leg higher and higher with each repetition as your pain allows. Doing this each day should hopefully free up the nerve a little bit and hopefully reduce some of your symptoms. In some respects that’s true. There is a problem.  What is your body trying to tell you? Is your physical condition good or do you have a poor posture? Are you stiff, tense, sore and restricted? Nerve impingement, entrapment, and sciatica are terms people often refer to when suffering with pain radiating into their limbs. When looking these up, people are often given the idea that discs pushing on nerves are the cause when, in reality, nerve irritation can occur anywhere along its path.  Just like a train route, nerve pathways are long and winding through intricate layers of tissues, through tunnels and grooves, and over active structures, which are dynamic and movable. All potential sites need to be explored when evaluating such conditions as tethering and entrapment don’t just happen at the spine.  In my experience, more likely than not, these symptoms are easily managed by appropriate assessment and treated using a tailored approach of integrated techniques. #sciaticnerve #backpain #fascia #rehabilitation #painrelief #sciatica #sciaticarelief #nerveimpingement #entrapment #nervepain #firecupping #cupping

Chronic pain, it’s easy to blame your nerves and say it’s all in your brain but consider the condition of your body, your muscles and your connective tissues.If you’ve got physical restrictions and reduce movement this generates pain signals. Fibromyalgia is not a neurological condition fibromyalgia is a result of using the wrong muscles and the stored trauma from inflammation events that you have been through, whatever they happen to be You’re not overly sensitive, it’s not your nervous system overreacting it’s because you have physical damage on your body. #fibromyalgia #chronicpain #nervepain #centralsensitizationsyndrome #medical #pain #nervoussystem #brainpain

2023… where do we start?! . You almost beat me, you tried your best, you beat me down, but I rose fighting💪🏼 . I think it’s fair to say that this year, I experienced the worst thing to ever happen to me. It’s taken so much from me and it’s made me fight harder than I’ve ever had to fight . But 2023… you didn’t beat me. I am stronger. I am braver. I am winning 🏆  . So in my standard New Years Eve fashion… . In 2023 I… - Went on multiple new adventures with friends ⛰️🥾 - Welcomed my 4th nephew into the world 🌍 👶🏻 - Rediscovered my love for running and ran better than ever before 🏃🏻‍♀️  - Signed up to 2 marathons! 🥇 - Watched my own baby turn from a boy to a man🧑🏻💙 - Went to Tenerife ✈️ with my gorgeous pals 💕 . But I also… - Had the worst accident of my life, where I broke and dislocated my hip, during a training run 🚑😥 - Spent a total of 6 weeks in hospital, learning to walk again and dealing with pain, that I simply cannot put into words 😖😭 - Had 3 general anaesthetics and gained 2 metal plates and 10 pins in my hip 💉🩸 - Learnt that the dislocation had caused permanent nerve damage to my leg and foot, leaving me permanently disabled 🩼  - Lost the whole summer and my holiday with Isaac 🥺 . But then I… - Put everything I had into my physio and grew stronger 💪🏼 - Rejoined the gym and found a new love in there 🏋🏻‍♀️ - Found a love also for swimming 🏊🏻‍♀️ - Learnt to start accepting and loving my new body for what it still was and what it still could achieve 🤍 - Got dressed up and went OUT OUT with my girls💃🏻 - Went to Lanzarote with my running family ✈️  - Discovered even more than I ready knew, how amazing my friends and family truly are, and of course Isaac 💙 . So, here’s to 2024! 🥂 May it be stronger, healthier and happier than ever 💪🏼💚☺️ . Want to ease sciatica at home? Try this exercise 👇 Nerve flossing (or neural gliding) is a simple way to mobilise painful nerves at home, and can be a helpful exercise to do at home as part of your treatment programme as a way to increase range of motion and reduce pain.  The sciatic nerve runs from the lower back, and can cause pain in your bum and all the way down to your foot. If you’ve got sciatic pain, try this sciatic nerve floss:  ⭐️Sitting nice and tall, feet flat on the floor. ⭐️ Extend one leg, toes pointing towards the ceiling ⭐️ As you do, extend your neck back to look at the ceiling ⭐️ Gently bring your leg back down, flexing your chin as you do. ⭐️ Bring the leg underneath you (past 90 degrees) and drop your chin to your chest.  Swap to the other leg. Repeat. Easy!  Ready to access our ultimate guide to managing sciatica?  Visit https://acorn-health.thinkific.com to find out more!  #sciatica #exercise #sciaticapain #sciaticarelief #chiropractic #sciaticnerve #nervepain #chiropractor #nerveflossing #backpain #legpain #injury #discinjury #sciaticpain #neural #Amesbury #Salisbury #Andover #Wiltshire #Wilton #sciaticarelief #sciaticpain #sciaticapainrelief #nerve #Wilton

Graston Therapy is a specialized form of soft tissue mobilization that utilizes precision-engineered instruments to address a variety of musculoskeletal issues. This therapeutic approach focuses on breaking down scar tissue, adhesions, and fascial restrictions within the body. By doing so, it aims to reduce pain, enhance circulation, and improve the overall function of soft tissues. The therapy is non-invasive, customizable, and often employed to complement other rehabilitation methods. Its benefits extend to athletes seeking improved performance, individuals recovering from injuries or surgeries, and those managing chronic conditions like tendonitis or plantar fasciitis. The technique is evidence-based, supported by research, and offers a versatile solution for promoting optimal movement, flexibility, and overall well-being. #grastontherapy #grastontechnique #deeptissuemassage #massage #treatment #therapy #pain #nervepain #sciatica #cupping

➡️ Treatment Spotlight - Low Level Laser Therapy, Red Light Therapy - Photobiomodulation.  ✅ We are one of the few clinics if not the only clinic in Central Scotland with the Thor Laser.  ➡️ What is PBMT❓ ➡️ PBMT / Cold Laser / Low Level Laser Therapy / Photobiomodulation Therapy  for healing and pain relief at STS.  ✅No extra cost  for PMB Therapy during your session ✅ There is substantial clinical evidence published in peer reviewed medical journals that Photobiomodulation (PBM Therapy) previously known as Low Level Laser Therapy (LLLT) can stimulate repair of tissue, reduce inflammation and relieve pain in musculoskeletal disorders. ➡️ The main areas with good evidence are: ✅ Soft Tissue Injuries ✅Joint conditions ✅ Back and Neck Pain ✅ Wound Healing Other applications such as shingles, post operative pain, also respond well. ➡️Laser and LED beams of light can stimulate the cells in the body that repair tissue, reduce inflammation and transmit pain. How Photobiomodulation Therapy works ➡️ Light can stimulate or inhibit cellular function according to it’s intensity and the time applied.✅ ➡️ Lasers and LED’s produce intense beams of light at specific wavelengths. When the right wavelength at the right intensity is used at the correct anatomical location for the right amount of time you can stimulate repair, resolve inflammation and reduce pain✅ ➡️ One of the primary mechanisms is the effect of light on cytochrome c oxidase and the consequently the unbinding of nitric oxide and release of ATP leading to improved cellular function. ✅ ➡️ For anti-inflammatory effects we have found a measurable reduction in PGE2, TNF Alpha and IL-6 in the synovia surrounding damaged tendons and for analgesia high intensity lasers over nerve supply can inhibit fast axonal flow.✅ @thorlaser  #lllt #pbmtherapy #photobiomodulation #lowlevellasertherapy #coldlaser #thorlaser #sportstherapyscotland #painmanagement #tissuerepair #atp #glasgow #stirling #sciatica #nervepain #arthritis #chronicpain #healing #backpain #headache #inflammation #sts #aclrepair #onset #cancer #painrelief #scotland

Replying to @m00npie  **Pregabalin: Important Information and Uses** **Warnings:** 1. **Hypersensitivity (Allergic) Reaction**:  This drug can lead to severe allergic reactions, such as breathing difficulties, rashes, and hives. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop taking it and seek immediate medical help. 2. **Suicidal Thoughts and Behavior**:  Pregabalin may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts and actions. Contact your doctor if you notice unusual mood changes, worsening depression, or thoughts of self-harm. 3. **Dizziness and Drowsiness**:  Pregabalin can cause dizziness, drowsiness, and blurred vision, impairing your ability to think and move. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. 4. **Misuse**:  Be cautious of misuse, especially if you have a history of drug misuse. Only take pregabalin as prescribed by your doctor. 5. **Respiratory Depression**:  If you use pregabalin along with central nervous system depressants like opioids, it can lead to severe breathing problems. Seek immediate medical help if you experience increased sleepiness or breathing difficulties. **What is Pregabalin?** - Pregabalin is a prescription drug available in capsule, solution, and extended-release tablet forms. This discussion focuses on the capsule form. - It is available as a generic drug and under the brand name Lyrica. - Pregabalin may be used alongside other medications, and its use is closely monitored due to its controlled substance status. **Why it's Used:** - Approved to treat neuropathic pain caused by damaged nerves (from diabetes, shingles, or spinal cord injury) in adults. - Effective for fibromyalgia (widespread body pain) in adults. - Used in combination with other seizure medications to manage partial onset seizures in individuals aged 17 and older. - In certain cases, doctors may prescribe it off-label for children under 17, which means for a purpose not officially approved. **How it Works:** - Pregabalin belongs to a class of drugs called anticonvulsants. - Its precise mechanism of action is unclear but is thought to involve calming damaged or overactive nerves that trigger pain or seizures. In summary, pregabalin is a prescription medication used to manage various conditions, but it carries important warnings regarding allergic reactions, potential for suicidal thoughts, dizziness, misuse, and respiratory issues when combined with certain medications. **Pregabalin: Important Information and Uses** **Warnings:** 1. **Hypersensitivity (Allergic) Reaction**:  This drug can lead to severe allergic reactions, such as breathing difficulties, rashes, and hives. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop taking it and seek immediate medical help. 2. **Suicidal Thoughts and Behavior**:  Pregabalin may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts and actions. Contact your doctor if you notice unusual mood changes, worsening depression, or thoughts of self-harm. 3. **Dizziness and Drowsiness**:  Pregabalin can cause dizziness, drowsiness, and blurred vision, impairing your ability to think and move. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. 4. **Misuse**:  Be cautious of misuse, especially if you have a history of drug misuse. Only take pregabalin as prescribed by your doctor. 5. **Respiratory Depression**:  If you use pregabalin along with central nervous system depressants like opioids, it can lead to severe breathing problems. Seek immediate medical help if you experience increased sleepiness or breathing difficulties. **What is Pregabalin?** - Pregabalin is a prescription drug available in capsule, solution, and extended-release tablet forms. This discussion focuses on the capsule form. - It is available as a generic drug and under the brand name Lyrica. - Pregabalin may be used alongside other medications, and its use is closely monitored due to its controlled substance status. **Why it's Used:** - Approved to treat neuropathic pain caused by damaged nerves (from diabetes, shingles, or spinal cord injury) in adults. - Effective for fibromyalgia (widespread body pain) in adults. - Used in combination with other seizure medications to manage partial onset seizures in individuals aged 17 and older. - In certain cases, doctors may prescribe it off-label for children under 17, which means for a purpose not officially approved. **How it Works:** - Pregabalin belongs to a class of drugs called anticonvulsants. - Its precise mechanism of action is unclear but is thought to involve calming damaged or overactive nerves that trigger pain or seizures. In summary, pregabalin is a prescription medication used to manage various conditions, but it carries important warnings regarding allergic reactions, potential for suicidal thoughts, dizziness, misuse, and respiratory issues when combined with certain medications. Always use it as directed by your doctor and be cautious about its effects on your alertness. #MedicationSafety  #HealthWarnings  #PainManagement #MentalHealthMatters #PrescriptionMeds #FibromyalgiaSupport  #SeizureControl #DrugEducation  #MedicalAwareness  #SafetyFirstTikTok  #pregabalin  #nervepain #chronicpain  #neuropathicpain #fybromyalgia #shingles  #diabetes  #seizures

Replying to @crazylife66676  Conquering Nerve Pain: A Guide for Daily Relief Pregabalin Research has shown that pregabalin can help in managing neuropathic (nerve) pain. It works by reducing the number of signals sent through the nerves. This medication is also used for epilepsy. Neuropathic pain is a type of pain that follows after damage to a nerve. It is thought to result from a “rewiring” of the nerves of the spinal cord. They are too sensitive and send too many pain signals. Normal touch can feel painful. There is often a “burning” or “shooting” feeling, or pins and needles. The pain can be there all the time or can come and go. How to take pregabalin The dose of pregabalin required varies from person to person. It should be taken regularly, usually, one capsule twice a day, with a gap of about 12 hours between doses. It can take up to 6-8 weeks to get the full benefit from pregabalin. Pregabalin comes in different strengths. The usual starting dose is 75mg twice a day. Some people will get benefit at this dose but others may require a higher dose. The dose can be increased gradually to a maximum of 300mg twice a day. How long should I take pregabalin for? In general, pregabalin will have to be taken for as long as you are requiring nerve pain relief. It should be reviewed every 6-12 months. Sometimes if someone has been taking pregabalin for a long time it may not work as well or may no longer be needed. If you, your doctor, pharmacist or pain specialist think this is happening they may help you reduce the dose slowly to see if you still need it. Do not stop taking your pregabalin suddenly if you have been taking it for a while. Your body may become used to the pregabalin and stopping it suddenly could cause withdrawal symptoms. Pregabalin has the potential to cause tolerance, dependence and addiction, although this is rare when taken as prescribed for chronic pain. This is more likely if they are or have been dependent on other drugs, alcohol or nicotine. Speak to your doctor, pharmacist or pain specialist if you have any concerns. Are there any side effects? All medicines can cause side effects but not everyone will get them. There is a full list in the patient information sheet with your prescription. Some side effects can be reduced by slowly building the dose. Others may pass after the first few doses.  If side effects go on and become a problem or you have others not expected then speak to your doctor, pharmacist or pain specialist. The most common side effects are drowsiness, dizziness, muscle fatigue and tremor. These side effects usually settle or reduce after a few days. If pregabalin makes you feel drowsy you should avoid driving or operating machinery. It is a criminal offence to drive a vehicle whilst unsafe due to medication use. This might be worse when you start the tablets and each time your dose goes up. Alcohol may make the sleepiness worse and should be avoided where possible. Less common side effects are visual disturbance, gastrointestinal upset, appetite changes, leg swelling, memory loss, mood changes or hallucinations and a rash. If you get these side effects contact your doctor, pharmacist or pain specialist for advice. If you experience any trouble breathing or are taking shallow breaths you should seek urgent medical help.  #MedicationSafety #HealthWarnings #PainManagement #MentalHealthMatters #PrescriptionMeds #FibromyalgiaSupport #SeizureControl#DrugEducation #MedicalAwareness #SafetyFirstTikTok #pregabalin #nervepain #chronicpain #neuropathicpain #fybromyalgia #shingles #diabetes #seizures

Hey mama, If you have hand and wrist pain, numbness or tingling you are probably suffering from Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTN). The syndrome is caused by compression of the median nerve in the wrist, leading to pain, numbness, and tingling in the hand and arm. During pregnancy, the hormonal changes that lead to fluid retention and the weight gain, increased pressure on the nerves, and swelling in the hands and wrists. I would advice you to perform daily wrist mobility exercises, do not force the movement and avoid pain. Nerves can get irritated if you overstretch them. Be gentle! Grip exercises can help to maintain the hand strength and also pump the swelling. You can practice 3setsx10 reps once a day (you can also use a ball). Wrist Splints can help during the night time, as they keep your wrist in a neutral position and this might reduce the nerve compression and manage swelling. ICE the wrist and hand for 15 minutes a few times a day (do not forget to roll the ice pack on a towel or cloth to protect your skin). I have been suffering from CTS for the past 2 months and these techniques have been helping me to manage all the pain and discomfort. I hope they work for you!🤞 Let me know if you have any question in the comments bellow🥰💕 #pregnancy #pregnancylife #pregnancytips #carpaltunnel #numbness #burningpain #physio #nervepain

Another day, another story of me being told something could not possibly be, when in reality if someone actually took the time to look ... the signs may have always been there. In January 2024 I had my first ever MRI (NHS)and then a few weeks later my endo specialist said I needed and MRI, I was like great I've already had one. But that MRI with the NHS had been of my upper spine and not around or on my pelvis. So I had a much more pleasant second MRI privately. Despite being diagnosed with endo in 2017, no one had ever done a MRI before or after diagnosis.  My mobility issues started after the very surgery that diagnosed me with Endo back in 2017, and so since then I've acquired a whole different variety of mobility aids. My life has had to be adapted, because it's had to. I was told it could be nerve pain or nerve damage by something burned in surgery, and that surgery always poses a risk for nerve damage. I remember first researching my nerve pain, looking more and more and seeing if it could be connected to endo. I remember finding out that endo on the spine could also cause nerve pain, and that's something that until that point I never knew. So I told the doctor my diagnosis, my new pains and could this be endo on my spine?  After being shut down, I foolishly never, ever asked again. I was then diagnosed with Fibromyalgia and Hypermobility and these new diagnosises because every doctors excuse for my mobility issues. And I'm not saying they haven't hugely contributed ... but imagine, just imagine ... if there was actually more to the story. 10 days until surgery, I wonder what they'll actually find. #sacral #extrapelvic #spine #nervepain #nervedamage #endometriosis #endo #endometriosisawarenessmonth #endoawarenessmonth #endo101 #endometriosis101 #periods #periodpain #menstrualhealth #womenshealth #1in10 #chronicillness #chronicallyill #fyp #foryoupage #advocacy #advocate #endoadvocate #endometriosisactionmonth #womenempowerwomen #womentiktok #infertility #fertility #fertilityjourney #ttc @Natalie | Endometriosis

Replying to @Esther Mcghee  Difference between Pregabalin & Gabapentin In the UK, both gabapentin and pregabalin are commonly prescribed medications. Here are some differences between the two based on UK data: Cost:  Generically, gabapentin is often less expensive than pregabalin. However, the cost can vary depending on factors such as the dosage, formulation, and whether the medication is obtained through the National Health Service (NHS) or purchased privately. Availability:  Both gabapentin and pregabalin are available in the UK, and they are commonly prescribed for various neuropathic pain conditions, including diabetic neuropathy, postherpetic neuralgia, and fibromyalgia.  Pregabalin is also licensed for the treatment of generalized anxiety disorder. Prescribing Regulations:  In the UK, pregabalin is classified as a Schedule 3 controlled drug under the Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001, whereas gabapentin is not a controlled drug. This means there are stricter regulations surrounding the prescribing and dispensing of pregabalin compared to gabapentin. Potency and Pharmacokinetics: Pregabalin is considered to be more potent than gabapentin. It has higher bioavailability and is absorbed more rapidly, leading to faster onset of action and more consistent plasma levels. Pregabalin also has a shorter elimination half-life compared to gabapentin. Indications:  Both gabapentin and pregabalin are approved for similar indications in the UK, including neuropathic pain conditions. However, pregabalin has additional licensed indications for generalized anxiety disorder and epilepsy. Side Effects:  While both medications have similar side effect profiles, individual responses may vary. Common side effects include dizziness, somnolence, peripheral edema, and weight gain.  Pregabalin may be associated with a higher incidence of certain side effects compared to gabapentin. Abuse Potential:  Pregabalin has been associated with a higher potential for misuse, dependence, and withdrawal symptoms compared to gabapentin. This has led to tighter regulations and monitoring of pregabalin prescriptions in the UK. Dosage and Administration:  Both gabapentin and pregabalin are available in various formulations, including capsules and oral solutions. Dosage and administration may vary depending on the indication, patient factors, and response to treatment. As always, it's essential to consult with a healthcare professional for personalized advice and guidance regarding the use of gabapentin and pregabalin. #pregabalin #gabapentin #depression #anxiety #anxietyrelief #pain #neuropathy #nervepain

WEIGHT GAIN Pregabalin can make you hungrier so it can be quite a challenge to stop yourself putting on weight.  Try to eat well without increasing your portion sizes. Do not snack on foods that contain a lot of calories, such as crisps, cakes, biscuits and sweets.  If you're hungry between meals, eat fruit and vegetables and low-calorie foods. Increasing your level of exercise will also help to keep your weight stable. **What is Pregabalin?** - Pregabalin is a prescription drug available in capsule, solution, and extended-release tablet forms. This discussion focuses on the capsule form. - It is available as a generic drug and under the brand name Lyrica. - Pregabalin may be used alongside other medications, and its use is closely monitored due to its controlled substance status. **Why it's Used:** - Approved to treat neuropathic pain caused by damaged nerves (from diabetes, shingles, or spinal cord injury) in adults. - Effective for fibromyalgia (widespread body pain) in adults. - Used in combination with other seizure medications to manage partial onset seizures in individuals aged 17 and older. - In certain cases, doctors may prescribe it off-label for children under 17, which means for a purpose not officially approved. **How it Works:** - Pregabalin belongs to a class of drugs called anticonvulsants. - Its precise mechanism of action is unclear but is thought to involve calming damaged or overactive nerves that trigger pain or seizures. In summary, pregabalin is a prescription medication used to manage various conditions, but it carries important warnings regarding allergic reactions, potential for suicidal thoughts, dizziness, misuse, and respiratory issues when combined with certain medications. Replying to @therajrpatel1  WHAT YOUR DR DOESN’T TELL YOU ABOUT PREGABALIN for pain relief & anxiety Pregabalin Research has shown that pregabalin can help in managing neuropathic (nerve) pain. It works by reducing the number of signals sent through the nerves. This medication is also used for epilepsy. Neuropathic pain is a type of pain that follows after damage to a nerve. It is thought to result from a “rewiring” of the nerves of the spinal cord. They are too sensitive and send too many pain signals. Normal touch can feel painful. There is often a “burning” or “shooting” feeling, or pins and needles. The pain can be there all the time or can come and go. How to take pregabalin The dose of pregabalin required varies from person to person. It should be taken regularly, usually, one capsule twice a day, with a gap of about 12 hours between doses. It can take up to 6-8 weeks to get the full benefit from pregabalin. Pregabalin comes in different strengths. The usual starting dose is 75mg twice a day. Some people will get benefit at this dose but others may require a higher dose. The dose can be increased gradually to a maximum of 300mg twice a day. How long should I take pregabalin for? In general, pregabalin will have to be taken for as long as you are requiring nerve pain relief. It should be reviewed every 6-12 months. Sometimes if someone has been taking pregabalin for a long time it may not work as well or may no longer be needed. If you, your doctor, pharmacist or pain specialist think this is happening they may help you reduce the dose slowly to see if you still need it. Do not stop taking your pregabalin suddenly if you have been taking it for a while. Your body may become used to the pregabalin and stopping it suddenly could cause withdrawal symptoms. Pregabalin has the potential to cause tolerance, dependence and addiction, although this is rare when taken as prescribed for chronic pain. This is more likely if they are or have been dependent on other drugs, alcohol or nicotine. Speak to your doctor, pharmacist or pain specialist if you have any concerns. Are there any side effects? All medicines can cause side effects but not everyone will get them. There is a full list in the patient information sheet with your prescription. Some side effects can be reduced by slowly building the dose. Others may pass after the first few doses. If side effects go on and become a problem or you have others not expected then speak to your doctor, pharmacist or pain specialist. The most common side effects are drowsiness, dizziness, muscle fatigue and tremor. These side effects usually settle or reduce after a few days. If pregabalin makes you feel drowsy you should avoid driving or operating machinery. It is a criminal offence to drive a vehicle whilst unsafe due to medication use. This might be worse when you start the tablets and each time your dose goes up. Alcohol may make the sleepiness worse and should be avoided where possible. Less common side effects are visual disturbance, gastrointestinal upset, appetite changes, leg swelling, memory loss, mood changes or hallucinations and a rash. If you get these side effects contact your doctor, pharmacist or pain specialist for advice. If you experience any trouble breathing or are taking shallow breaths you should seek urgent medical help.  #MedicationSafety #HealthWarnings #PainManagement #MentalHealthMatters #PrescriptionMeds #FibromyalgiaSupport #SeizureControl#DrugEducation #MedicalAwareness #SafetyFirstTikTok #pregabalin #nervepain #chronicpain #neuropathicpain #fybromyalgia #shingles #diabetes #seizures

Just a CBT document.  🧠 My ME was at its worst between September 2017-March 2018, I thought I could push through but the reality is, dont. ME is the only condition where exercise has devestating consequences.  🧠 2024, the year my bladder cut out. Replying to @Andrea 🍒  **Pregabalin: Important Information and Uses** **Warnings:** 1. **Hypersensitivity (Allergic) Reaction**:  This drug can lead to severe allergic reactions, such as breathing difficulties, rashes, and hives. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop taking it and seek immediate medical help. 2. **Suicidal Thoughts and Behavior**:  Pregabalin may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts and actions. Contact your doctor if you notice unusual mood changes, worsening depression, or thoughts of self-harm. 3. **Dizziness and Drowsiness**:  Pregabalin can cause dizziness, drowsiness, and blurred vision, impairing your ability to think and move. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. 4. **Misuse**:  Be cautious of misuse, especially if you have a history of drug misuse. Only take pregabalin as prescribed by your doctor. 5. **Respiratory Depression**:  If you use pregabalin along with central nervous system depressants like opioids, it can lead to severe breathing problems. Seek immediate medical help if you experience increased sleepiness or breathing difficulties. **What is Pregabalin?** - Pregabalin is a prescription drug available in capsule, solution, and extended-release tablet forms. This discussion focuses on the capsule form. - It is available as a generic drug and under the brand name Lyrica. - Pregabalin may be used alongside other medications, and its use is closely monitored due to its controlled substance status. **Why it's Used:** - Approved to treat neuropathic pain caused by damaged nerves (from diabetes, shingles, or spinal cord injury) in adults. - Effective for fibromyalgia (widespread body pain) in adults. - Used in combination with other seizure medications to manage partial onset seizures in individuals aged 17 and older. - In certain cases, doctors may prescribe it off-label for children under 17, which means for a purpose not officially approved. **How it Works:** - Pregabalin belongs to a class of drugs called anticonvulsants. - Its precise mechanism of action is unclear but is thought to involve calming damaged or overactive nerves that trigger pain or seizures. In summary, pregabalin is a prescription medication used to manage various conditions, but it carries important warnings regarding allergic reactions, potential for suicidal thoughts, dizziness, misuse, and respiratory issues when combined with certain medications. Always use it as directed by your doctor and be cautious about its effects on your alertness. #MedicationSafety  #HealthWarnings  #PainManagement #MentalHealthMatters #PrescriptionMeds #FibromyalgiaSupport  #SeizureControl #DrugEducation  #MedicalAwareness  #SafetyFirstTikTok  #pregabalin  #nervepain #chronicpain  #neuropathicpain #fybromyalgia #shingles #epilepsy #depression #anxietydisorder  #diabetes  #seizures

PREGABALIN SERIOUS SIDE EFFECTS **Pregabalin: Important Information and Uses** **Warnings:** 1. **Hypersensitivity (Allergic) Reaction**:  This drug can lead to severe allergic reactions, such as breathing difficulties, rashes, and hives. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop taking it and seek immediate medical help. 2. **Suicidal Thoughts and Behavior**:  Pregabalin may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts and actions. Contact your doctor if you notice unusual mood changes, worsening depression, or thoughts of self-harm. 3. **Dizziness and Drowsiness**:  Pregabalin can cause dizziness, drowsiness, and blurred vision, impairing your ability to think and move. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. 4. **Misuse**:  Be cautious of misuse, especially if you have a history of drug misuse. Only take pregabalin as prescribed by your doctor. 5. **Respiratory Depression**:  If you use pregabalin along with central nervous system depressants like opioids, it can lead to severe breathing problems. Seek immediate medical help if you experience increased sleepiness or breathing difficulties. **What is Pregabalin?** - Pregabalin is a prescription drug available in capsule, solution, and extended-release tablet forms. This discussion focuses on the capsule form. - It is available as a generic drug and under the brand name Lyrica. - Pregabalin may be used alongside other medications, and its use is closely monitored due to its controlled substance status. **Why it's Used:** - Approved to treat neuropathic pain caused by damaged nerves (from diabetes, shingles, or spinal cord injury) in adults. - Effective for fibromyalgia (widespread body pain) in adults. - Used in combination with other seizure medications to manage partial onset seizures in individuals aged 17 and older. - In certain cases, doctors may prescribe it off-label for children under 17, which means for a purpose not officially approved. **How it Works:** - Pregabalin belongs to a class of drugs called anticonvulsants. - Its precise mechanism of action is unclear but is thought to involve calming damaged or overactive nerves that trigger pain or seizures. In summary, pregabalin is a prescription medication used to manage various conditions, but it carries important warnings regarding allergic reactions, potential for suicidal thoughts, dizziness, misuse, and respiratory issues when combined with certain medications. Always use it as directed by your doctor and be cautious about its effects on your alertness. #MedicationSafety  #HealthWarnings  #PainManagement #MentalHealthMatters #PrescriptionMeds #FibromyalgiaSupport  #SeizureControl #DrugEducation  #MedicalAwareness  #SafetyFirstTikTok  #pregabalin  #nervepain #chronicpain  #neuropathicpain #fybromyalgia #shingles  #diabetes  #seizures

Pregabalin DANGEROUS side effects!  Research has shown that pregabalin can help in managing neuropathic (nerve) pain. It works by reducing the number of signals sent through the nerves. This medication is also used for epilepsy. Neuropathic pain is a type of pain that follows after damage to a nerve. It is thought to result from a “rewiring” of the nerves of the spinal cord. They are too sensitive and send too many pain signals. Normal touch can feel painful. There is often a “burning” or “shooting” feeling, or pins and needles. The pain can be there all the time or can come and go. How to take pregabalin The dose of pregabalin required varies from person to person. It should be taken regularly, usually, one capsule twice a day, with a gap of about 12 hours between doses. It can take up to 6-8 weeks to get the full benefit from pregabalin. Pregabalin comes in different strengths. The usual starting dose is 75mg twice a day. Some people will get benefit at this dose but others may require a higher dose. The dose can be increased gradually to a maximum of 300mg twice a day. How long should I take pregabalin for? In general, pregabalin will have to be taken for as long as you are requiring nerve pain relief. It should be reviewed every 6-12 months. Sometimes if someone has been taking pregabalin for a long time it may not work as well or may no longer be needed. If you, your doctor, pharmacist or pain specialist think this is happening they may help you reduce the dose slowly to see if you still need it. Do not stop taking your pregabalin suddenly if you have been taking it for a while. Your body may become used to the pregabalin and stopping it suddenly could cause withdrawal symptoms. Pregabalin has the potential to cause tolerance, dependence and addiction, although this is rare when taken as prescribed for chronic pain. This is more likely if they are or have been dependent on other drugs, alcohol or nicotine. Speak to your doctor, pharmacist or pain specialist if you have any concerns. Are there any side effects? All medicines can cause side effects but not everyone will get them. There is a full list in the patient information sheet with your prescription. Some side effects can be reduced by slowly building the dose. Others may pass after the first few doses. If side effects go on and become a problem or you have others not expected then speak to your doctor, pharmacist or pain specialist. The most common side effects are drowsiness, dizziness, muscle fatigue and tremor. These side effects usually settle or reduce after a few days. If pregabalin makes you feel drowsy you should avoid driving or operating machinery. It is a criminal offence to drive a vehicle whilst unsafe due to medication use. This might be worse when you start the tablets and each time your dose goes up. Alcohol may make the sleepiness worse and should be avoided where possible. Less common side effects are visual disturbance, gastrointestinal upset, appetite changes, leg swelling, memory loss, mood changes or hallucinations and a rash. If you get these side effects contact your doctor, pharmacist or pain specialist for advice. If you experience any trouble breathing or are taking shallow breaths you should seek urgent medical help.  #MedicationSafety #HealthWarnings #PainManagement #MentalHealthMatters #PrescriptionMeds #FibromyalgiaSupport #SeizureControl#DrugEducation #MedicalAwareness #SafetyFirstTikTok #pregabalin #nervepain #chronicpain #neuropathicpain #fybromyalgia #shingles #diabetes #seizures #anxiety

Small fibre neuropathy  Nerves comprise two fibres: large fibres going to our muscles and small fibres carrying sensation information to our central nervous system. Small fibre neuropathy is where only the small fibres are altered or damaged. This leads to burning, pins and needles or stabbing pain without muscle changes, such as weakness. The most common form is called a length-dependent presentation, where the feet are affected first; this is commonly seen as a complication of diabetes. Around 15% of individuals may get a patchy/diffuse distribution. This form is associated with an autoimmune cause and may be misdiagnosed as fibromyalgia. The treatment involves improving the underlying causes, such as diabetes or autoimmune conditions. This is coupled with pain management medications and non-pharmacologic treatments such as heat, ice and TENS machines. #neuropathy #diabetes #fibromyalgia #pain #neurology

Those who are especially sensitive tend to get stuck in our limiting beliefs, preventing us from living our best lives. This doesn't have to be the case, though. Let's discuss five quotes that people like you and me frequently return to when they're struggling to cope with their limiting beliefs. Remember, these quotes aren't just phrases—they can help guide you toward personal growth and self-compassion. As we review these quotes, you can reflect on their meanings and how you can apply them to your life. 1. "Believe That You Can and You're Halfway There." - Theodore Roosevelt Theodore Roosevelt emphasizes the significance of self-confidence and positive thinking in this quote. He suggests that a strong belief in your abilities is a driving force and can help push you closer to achieving your goals. In simpler terms, you must have a positive mindset and believe in yourself when facing challenges and working towards your goals. 2. "The Mind is Everything. What You Think You Become" - Buddha Here, Buddha talks about how attitude plays a significant role in determining one's identity. In a way, we are our thoughts, which influence our identity and experiences. This is why it's essential to be mindful and consider how giving in to negative thoughts can impact personal growth. 3. "You Must Find the Place Inside Yourself Where Nothing is Impossible." - Deepak Chopra We have untapped potential, and Deepak Chopra's quote emphasizes this. You must believe nothing is impossible and chase your goals to the best of your abilities. Digging deep to find this "place where nothing is impossible" will take some work, but it'll help you build up your resilience, so it's well worth it. 4. "Do Not Be Embarrassed By Your Failures, Learn From Them and Start Again" - Richard Branson Perhaps you've heard the fable of the crow who, after failing to get water out of a bottle, started putting stones into the bottle to make the water level rise. The moral of this fable is: "If at first you don't succeed, try, try again." Richard Branson is saying something similar here. If you allow yourself to be so embarrassed by your failures that you never try again, you'll be inadvertently limiting yourself. Instead of getting embarrassed, learn from your failures, and you'll eventually achieve success. 5. "Don't Be Pushed Around By the Fears in Your Mind. Be Led By the Dreams in Your Heart." - Roy T. Bennett This quote urges people to push back against the fears that might hold them back and focus on their dreams instead. It suggests adopting a mindset that values passion and vision more than your perceived limits set by your fears. The idea is to follow your heart rather than allow yourself to be controlled by your worries. In other words, don't let your anxiety and thoughts of self-doubt get in the way of pursuing your passions. Why Are These Quotes Important? When times are tough, people often need something to look to. This is why these quotes have been documented over time. Replying to @Amanda Taylor  PREGABALIN WITHDRAWL & HARMFUL EFFECTS  **Pregabalin: Important Information and Uses** **Warnings:** 1. **Hypersensitivity (Allergic) Reaction**:  This drug can lead to severe allergic reactions, such as breathing difficulties, rashes, and hives. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop taking it and seek immediate medical help. 2. **Suicidal Thoughts and Behavior**:  Pregabalin may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts and actions. Contact your doctor if you notice unusual mood changes, worsening depression, or thoughts of self-harm. 3. **Dizziness and Drowsiness**:  Pregabalin can cause dizziness, drowsiness, and blurred vision, impairing your ability to think and move. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. 4. **Misuse**:  Be cautious of misuse, especially if you have a history of drug misuse. Only take pregabalin as prescribed by your doctor. 5. **Respiratory Depression**:  If you use pregabalin along with central nervous system depressants like opioids, it can lead to severe breathing problems. Seek immediate medical help if you experience increased sleepiness or breathing difficulties. **What is Pregabalin?** - Pregabalin is a prescription drug available in capsule, solution, and extended-release tablet forms. This discussion focuses on the capsule form. - It is available as a generic drug and under the brand name Lyrica. - Pregabalin may be used alongside other medications, and its use is closely monitored due to its controlled substance status. **Why it's Used:** - Approved to treat neuropathic pain caused by damaged nerves (from diabetes, shingles, or spinal cord injury) in adults. - Effective for fibromyalgia (widespread body pain) in adults. - Used in combination with other seizure medications to manage partial onset seizures in individuals aged 17 and older. - In certain cases, doctors may prescribe it off-label for children under 17, which means for a purpose not officially approved. **How it Works:** - Pregabalin belongs to a class of drugs called anticonvulsants. - Its precise mechanism of action is unclear but is thought to involve calming damaged or overactive nerves that trigger pain or seizures. In summary, pregabalin is a prescription medication used to manage various conditions, but it carries important warnings regarding allergic reactions, potential for suicidal thoughts, dizziness, misuse, and respiratory issues when combined with certain medications. Its not always ‘old’ people who have pernicious anaemia, my symptoms over the past 12/13 years have been labelled as a whole host of other stuff, GERD (because they couldn’t find the reason for my gut issues) then it was down to the stress in my life mainly caring for my autistic son leading to burnout, allergies & fatigue put down to mould exposure from living in a damp house (rising damp the council are reluctant to fix), folate anaemia. I then seriously broke my ankle/leg (open ankle fracture 🤢) nerve damage symptoms put down to that. Fatigue, low mobility leg pains , balance problems all put doen to my ankle injury, even when the nerve issues started affecting the other uninjured leg, put down to the nerve damage. Then the painkillers for the nerve pain stopped working on the ‘good’ leg……. turns out i have pernicious anaemia & cant absorb vitamin b12! Replying to @Tiff Van Haylett  PREGABALIN SERIOUS SIDE EFFECTS  **Pregabalin: Important Information and Uses** **Warnings:** 1. **Hypersensitivity (Allergic) Reaction**:  This drug can lead to severe allergic reactions, such as breathing difficulties, rashes, and hives. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop taking it and seek immediate medical help. 2. **Suicidal Thoughts and Behavior**:  Pregabalin may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts and actions. Contact your doctor if you notice unusual mood changes, worsening depression, or thoughts of self-harm. 3. **Dizziness and Drowsiness**:  Pregabalin can cause dizziness, drowsiness, and blurred vision, impairing your ability to think and move. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. 4. **Misuse**:  Be cautious of misuse, especially if you have a history of drug misuse. Only take pregabalin as prescribed by your doctor. 5. **Respiratory Depression**:  If you use pregabalin along with central nervous system depressants like opioids, it can lead to severe breathing problems. Seek immediate medical help if you experience increased sleepiness or breathing difficulties. **What is Pregabalin?** - Pregabalin is a prescription drug available in capsule, solution, and extended-release tablet forms. This discussion focuses on the capsule form. - It is available as a generic drug and under the brand name Lyrica. - Pregabalin may be used alongside other medications, and its use is closely monitored due to its controlled substance status. **Why it's Used:** - Approved to treat neuropathic pain caused by damaged nerves (from diabetes, shingles, or spinal cord injury) in adults. - Effective for fibromyalgia (widespread body pain) in adults. - Used in combination with other seizure medications to manage partial onset seizures in individuals aged 17 and older. - In certain cases, doctors may prescribe it off-label for children under 17, which means for a purpose not officially approved. **How it Works:** - Pregabalin belongs to a class of drugs called anticonvulsants. - Its precise mechanism of action is unclear but is thought to involve calming damaged or overactive nerves that trigger pain or seizures. In summary, pregabalin is a prescription medication used to manage various conditions, but it carries important warnings regarding allergic reactions, potential for suicidal thoughts, dizziness, misuse, and respiratory issues when combined with certain medications. **Pregabalin: Important Information and Uses** **Warnings:** 1. **Hypersensitivity (Allergic) Reaction**:  This drug can lead to severe allergic reactions, such as breathing difficulties, rashes, and hives. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop taking it and seek immediate medical help. 2. **Suiczidal Thoughts and Behaviour**:  Pregabalin may increase the risk of suizidal thoughts and actions. Contact your doctor if you notice unusual mood changes, worsening depression, or thoughts of self-harm. 3. **Dizziness and Drowsiness**:  Pregabalin can cause dizziness, drowsiness, and blurred vision, impairing your ability to think and move. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. 4. **Misuse**:  Be cautious of misuse, especially if you have a history of drug misuse. Only take pregabalin as prescribed by your doctor. 5. **Respiratory Depression**:  If you use pregabalin along with central nervous system depressants like opioids, it can lead to severe breathing problems. Seek immediate medical help if you experience increased sleepiness or breathing difficulties. **What is Pregabalin?** - Pregabalin is a prescription drug available in capsule, solution, and extended-release tablet forms. This discussion focuses on the capsule form. - It is available as a generic drug and under the brand name Lyrica. - Pregabalin may be used alongside other medications, and its use is closely monitored due to its controlled substance status. **Why it's Used:** - Approved to treat neuropathic pain caused by damaged nerves (from diabetes, shingles, or spinal cord injury) in adults. - Effective for fibromyalgia (widespread body pain) in adults. - Used in combination with other seizure medications to manage partial onset seizures in individuals aged 17 and older. - In certain cases, doctors may prescribe it off-label for children under 17, which means for a purpose not officially approved. **How it Works:** - Pregabalin belongs to a class of drugs called anticonvulsants. - Its precise mechanism of action is unclear but is thought to involve calming damaged or overactive nerves that trigger pain or seizures. In summary, pregabalin is a prescription medication used to manage various conditions, but it carries important warnings regarding allergic reactions, potential for suicidal thoughts, dizziness, misuse, and respiratory issues when combined with certain medications. HOW TO STOP PREGABALIN SAFELY  Tapering off pregabalin should always be done under the supervision of a healthcare provider to ensure safety and minimize withdrawal symptoms. Here are some general guidelines for tapering off pregabalin: 1. **Consult Your Healthcare Provider:** Before making any changes to your medication, discuss your plan with your doctor. They will provide a tapering schedule tailored to your specific needs. 2. **Gradual Reduction:** Tapering off pregabalin typically involves gradually reducing the dose over a period of time. This helps your body adjust and reduces the risk of withdrawal symptoms. 3. **Typical Tapering Schedule:** While the exact schedule will depend on your current dose, duration of use, and individual response, a common approach might look like this:     - Reduce the daily dose by 10-25% every 1-2 weeks.     - Continue this process until you are completely off the medication. 4. **Monitor for Withdrawal Symptoms:** Be aware of potential withdrawal symptoms, which can include anxiety, insomnia, nausea, headaches, and increased pain. If you experience severe symptoms, contact your healthcare provider immediately. 5. **Adjust as Necessary:** Your doctor may adjust the tapering schedule based on your response. Some people may need a slower tapering process. 6. **Supportive Care:** Engage in supportive care practices such as staying hydrated, maintaining a healthy diet, and practicing stress-reduction techniques like meditation or gentle exercise. 7. **Follow-Up:** Regular follow-up appointments with your healthcare provider are important to monitor your progress and make any necessary adjustments to your tapering schedule. SERIOUS SIDE EFFECTS OF PREGABALIN Important Information and Uses **Warnings:** 1. **Hypersensitivity (Allergic) Reaction**:  This drug can lead to severe allergic reactions, such as breathing difficulties, rashes, and hives. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop taking it and seek immediate medical help. 2. **Untoward Thoughts and Behaviour**:  Pregabalin may increase the risk of untoward thoughts and actions. Contact your doctor if you notice unusual mood changes, worsening depression, or thoughts of self-harm. 3. **Dizziness and Drowsiness**:  Pregabalin can cause dizziness, drowsiness, and blurred vision, impairing your ability to think and move. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. 4. **Misuse**:  Be cautious of misuse, especially if you have a history of drug misuse. Only take pregabalin as prescribed by your doctor. 5. **Respiratory Depression**:  If you use pregabalin along with central nervous system depressants like opioids, it can lead to severe breathing problems. Seek immediate medical help if you experience increased sleepiness or breathing difficulties. **What is Pregabalin?** - Pregabalin is a prescription drug available in capsule, solution, and extended-release tablet forms. This discussion focuses on the capsule form. - It is available as a generic drug and under the brand name Lyrica. - Pregabalin may be used alongside other medications, and its use is closely monitored due to its controlled substance status. **Why it's Used:** - Approved to treat neuropathic pain caused by damaged nerves (from diabetes, shingles, or spinal cord injury) in adults. - Effective for fibromyalgia (widespread body pain) in adults. - Used in combination with other seizure medications to manage partial onset seizures in individuals aged 17 and older. - In certain cases, doctors may prescribe it off-label for children under 17, which means for a purpose not officially approved. **How it Works:** - Pregabalin belongs to a class of drugs called anticonvulsants. - Its precise mechanism of action is unclear but is thought to involve calming damaged or overactive nerves that trigger pain or seizures. In summary, pregabalin is a prescription medication used to manage various conditions, but it carries important warnings regarding allergic reactions, potential for suicidal thoughts, dizziness, misuse, and respiratory issues when combined with certain medications. Vitamin B12 Deficiency in Clinical Practice: "Doctor, you gave me my life back!" Dr Joseph Chandy Kayyalackakom MD The full book available for free to download  https://www.b12d.org/book A Journey Through Key Figures in History: Key Figures in  History: James Combe (1796-1883): First reported severe anaemia cases with atrophic gastritis. Thomas Addison (1793-1860): Identified megaloblastic anaemia, leading to 'Addison-Biermer's disease.' George Whipple (1878-1976), George Minot (1885-1950), William Murphy (1892-1987): Discovered liver's role in treating anaemia, leading to Nobel Prize-winning work. Dorothy Hodgkin (1910-1994): Defined the structure of vitamin B12. In the 19th century, when PA was first identified,  Scientific Advances: From raw liver treatments in the 1920s to isolating vitamin B12 in the 1940s, and recognising PA as an autoimmune disease in the 1960s, scientific progress has transformed from a fatal disease to a manageable condition. What is Pernicious Anaemia? Pernicious Anaemia (PA) is NOT a dietary B12 deficiency but a serious autoimmune condition. It inhibits the body's ability to absorb B12, leading to cobalamin deficiency, atrophy of the stomach lining, and megaloblastic anaemia. This results in red blood cells that are unable to efficiently carry oxygen throughout the body. DEFFERENCES IN ANXIETY NERVE PAIN MEDICATION  Certainly! Here are some key scientific differences between Lyrica (pregabalin) and gabapentin: 	1.	Chemical Structure: 	•	Lyrica is chemically known as pregabalin, while gabapentin is chemically distinct as gabapentinoid. 	2.	Absorption and Onset of Action: 	•	Lyrica is absorbed more rapidly and has a faster onset of action compared to gabapentin. This means it reaches therapeutic levels in the bloodstream more quickly after ingestion. 	3.	Bioavailability: 	•	Lyrica has higher bioavailability than gabapentin, meaning a greater proportion of the drug is absorbed into the bloodstream and is available to exert its effects. 	4.	Half-life: 	•	Lyrica has a shorter elimination half-life compared to gabapentin. This means it is metabolized and cleared from the body more quickly. 	5.	Dosage Flexibility: 	•	Gabapentin is available in more diverse dosage forms, including capsules, tablets, and oral solutions, whereas Lyrica is primarily available as capsules and oral solutions. 	6.	Potency: 	•	While both drugs are effective in treating neuropathic pain and seizures, there is no clear evidence suggesting that one is inherently more potent than the other. Efficacy may vary from person to person. 	7.	Cost: 	•	Lyrica tends to be more expensive than gabapentin, especially considering that gabapentin is available in generic form. Cost can vary depending on factors such as insurance coverage and pharmacy pricing. 	8.	Side Effect Profile: 	•	While both medications share common side effects such as dizziness, drowsiness, and weight gain, individual patients may experience different side effect profiles with each drug due to their unique pharmacokinetics and mechanisms of action. These differences can influence factors such as dosing regimens, onset of action, and cost, and may be considered by healthcare providers when choosing between Lyrica and gabapentin for a particular patient’s treatment. #anxiety #depression #depressionanxiety #depressionawareness #nervepain #shingles #pregabalin #gabapentin #depression #anxiety #anxietyrelief #pain #neuropathy #nervepain

Sciatica is a deep and foundational pain which prevents forward movement. Nerve pain is related to communication And so it’s likely that the enduring pain of sciatica is linked to communication difficulties with family relationships. Behind the pain is tension, tightness and imbalance. What was happening before the onset of the pain? Maybe you don’t feel heard or understood or maybe you feel undermined , manipulated or disconnected from the people you desire love and support from. The message from your body is about pausing to re evaluate and realign your direction in life. What has become uncomfortable? In what ways are you compromising your SELF so that others stay happy with you? If you continue on the path that you are currently walking… where will that take you? Is that something you want for yourself? Sciatic pain creates change and learning - can you notice the tension and what triggers it? Change is often the cause and the outcome of pain. Ponder on the changes you see, desire or resist in your life. In those thoughts you will find the reason for the pain. Finding the Root Cause is the healing journey. #sciatica #nervepain #communicationdifficulties #tension #unheard #directioninlife #selfcompromise #HealingJourney

But actually that’s not the case at all. I’m forever doing admin for my complex health I am currently under 20+ different specialists that are up and down the country and unfortunately they don’t all communicate to one another and don’t oversee my care holistically and therefore I am forever relaying information back and forth between these doctors to ensure nothing is lost in transition because it can become quickly confusing 🫤 it’s a bit like Chinease whispers if you don’t keep track of what’s being relayed then things will soon get muddled or changed so you’re always on guard ensuring things are done, constantly chasing referrals and attending MDT meetings for your on going deteriorating health and chasing doctors for letters and for referrals new medications, new treatment plans etc etc the list goes on. But most people when they come home from work their work is over… ours is NEVER OVER, we can’t just wake up one day and be like I need a me day and then do that we are constantly dictated by our health needs and don’t get to necessarily spend the days doing what we please when we please it’s currently 4am here and I’ve been woken up with burning urine and burning pain that radiates all around my lower back and stomach and today I have a busy schedule of health appointments and other commitments I however cannot just cancel all of this as it will impact my care now and further down the line and will have to push through I can’t just not do my job my job is 24/7 and it’s caring for my health and needs, so I may not necessarily get up and go to work but every day I spend it doing work and looking after my complex multisystemic diseases all while trying to live a somewhat normal life. I’m on so many meds to control so many complex symptoms it wouldn’t be possible for me to hold down a job as I’m so poorly 90% of the time it’s hard to keep myself well let alone hold down a “job” and do life as well being chronically ill isn’t just getting to stay at home all day, it’s staying at home all day fighting against your own body who is trying to constantly off you 24/7 it’s about symptoms management 24/7 constantly questioning if you do anything questioning if that is going to cause you a flare in symptoms or if it’s worth doing that task, it’s isolation from the general public, it’s isolation from a social group that you would naturally form whilst in employment, it’s loosing friends because you can keep up with them socially because you are too ill to see them or in too much pain to see them or you just simply can’t due to being in out of hospital all of the time. Being chronically ill is hard and tough! But actually that’s not the case at all. I’m forever doing admin for my complex health I am currently under 20+ different specialists that are up and down the country and unfortunately they don’t all communicate to one another and don’t oversee my care holistically and therefore I am forever relaying information back and forth between these doctors to ensure nothing is lost in transition because it can become quickly confusing 🫤 it’s a bit like Chinease whispers if you don’t keep track of what’s being relayed then things will soon get muddled or changed so you’re always on guard ensuring things are done, constantly chasing referrals and attending MDT meetings for your on going deteriorating health and chasing doctors for letters and for referrals new medications, new treatment plans etc etc the list goes on. But most people when they come home from work their work is over… ours is NEVER OVER, we can’t just wake up one day and be like I need a me day and then do that we are constantly dictated by our health needs and don’t get to necessarily spend the days doing what we please when we please it’s currently 4am here and I’ve been woken up with burning urine and burning pain that radiates all around my lower back and stomach and today I have a busy schedule of health appointments and other commitments I however cannot just cancel all of this as it will impact my care now and further down the line and will have to push through I can’t just not do my job my job is 24/7 and it’s caring for my health and needs, so I may not necessarily get up and go to work but every day I spend it doing work and looking after my complex multisystemic diseases all while trying to live a somewhat normal life. I’m on so many meds to control so many complex symptoms it wouldn’t be possible for me to hold down a job as I’m so poorly 90% of the time it’s hard to keep myself well let alone hold down a “job” and do life as well being chronically ill isn’t just getting to stay at home all day, it’s staying at home all day fighting against your own body who is trying to constantly off you 24/7 it’s about symptoms management 24/7 constantly questioning if you do anything questioning if that is going to cause you a flare in symptoms or if it’s worth doing that task, it’s isolation from the general public, it’s isolation from a social group that you would naturally form whilst in employment, it’s loosing friends because you can keep up with them socially because you are too ill to see them or in too much pain to see them or you just simply can’t due to being in out of hospital all of the time. Being chronically ill is hard and tough! But I know that despite all of these challenges I face like so many others I still have a wonderful beautiful life amongst all of the medical craziness I still love my little life! #medicallycomplex #heds #eds #disabilityawareness #loneliness #socialisolation #disabled #chronicallyill #disabilityawareness #disabilityadvocate #disabilityrights #disabilityadvocacy #disablityandme #disabilitytiktok #ehlersdanlossyndrome #brittleasthma #mcas #gastroparesis #scoliosis #intestinaldysmotility #gerd #adhd #autism #jointhypermobility #liagmentdamage #nervepain #neurogenicbladder #bladderpain #bladderdisorder #incontinence #beautifullydisabled #eds #loveyouall #staypositive #fyp

Muscles tighten in defence. This was a conversation about nerve pain and Sciatica from our most recent RCP course. Different emotions can exist in us at the same moment. We have layers of thoughts, different parts, all talking at once. Those very deepest layers are often an undercurrent to our lives, directing our responses. When anger, frustration or resentment is activated and triggered in us then Fear is often sitting below at this deep level of our consciousness. Anger is the defence, the armour, the knee-jerk reaction. This is what creates the tightening and hardening that often leads to rigidity and pain. The fear below that can be difficult to bring awareness to. I can give you a personal example - years ago my back went into a painful spasm the day after a family birthday celebration. This was familiar as I often felt frustrated and tense around my family, always preparing myself for the little put downs or comments that made me feel like I had to defend myself. Back then I wouldn’t have recognised the fear below the anger - that understanding came later. I now have the awareness that the truth was that their comments hurt and always had. I had learnt to harden my heart in order to protect my vulnerability. The question that unlocks the fear is - what would happen if I didn’t harden and defend myself? For me that meant the hurt would be seen, the pain would be on show and from experience that meant more separation - emotions were not welcome, understood or acknowledged. It was safer to hold in than to express. These are the patterns formed in childhood that continue to play out in adulthood. ✨✨ New Beta course on changing patterns coming soon.✨✨ #Musclespasm #NervePain #Sciatica #rootcause #emotionallayers #angerdefendspain #fearactivation #FamilyTension #vulnerability #changingpatterns #rigidity #rootcause #emotionalanatomy #mindbodyconnection

FLY AGARIC - AMANITA MUSCARIA This well know mushroom have a very controversial reputation. A lot of mushroom foraging books will classify this mushroom as poisonous . This is because it’s compound called Ibotenic acid has shown some potential neurotoxicity. Nevertheless, Ibotenic acid degrades when the mushroom gets dried or exposed to heat.  The use of fly agaric as an entheogen has been very well documented  in populations all over Europe and northern Asia. It is said that the myth of Santa Claus has its roots in the ceremonial use of this mushroom. Medicinally, fly agarics can be used to as a topical balm or tincture too, resolve the symptoms of neuralgia, such as in sciatica or nerve impingement. ##FlyAgaric ##WildMushrooms##MagicMedicine##Foraging##Herbalist##Herbalism##HerbalMedicine##Herbology##Sciatica##Nervepain

Pernicious anaemia is a disease where not enough red blood cells are produced due to a deficiency of vitamin B12. Those affected often have a gradual onset. The most common initial symptoms are feeling tired and weak. My first symptoms were feeling absolutely "washed out." Even though I've got multiple chronic illnesses including ME/Chronic fatigue, it was a more lifeless and weak feeling on top of my usual fatigue. I also noticed a very sore mouth, mouth ulcers, and cracks on my tongue. My mouth would sting if I ate and drank, and I had a burning feeling in my mouth all of the time. I also felt more down than usual and almost lost for words that I wanted to say during conversations. The words were there somewhere but didn't come to mind as they should. Again, I suffer this foggy type of feeling (Brain fog) anyway with my other conditions but it was much more noticeable. I could almost speak a sentence backwards with words missing. If vitamin B12 deficiency is left untreated, it can cause lasting side effects that affect the nervous system and brain, As a guidance here is a list of symptoms that may occur if you are B12 deficient. Vitamin B12 deficiency can also cause symptoms that affect your brain and nervous system (neurological symptoms), including: ● Numbness ● Muscle weakness ● Psychological problems which can range from mild depression or anxiety, to confusion and dementia ● Problems with balance and coordination ● Pins and needles ●  Incontinence indigestion ● Loss of appetite ● Palpitations ● Problems with your vision ● Feeling weak or tired ●Diarrhoea ●A sore or red tongue, sometimes with mouth ulcers ●Problems with memory understanding and judgment (cognitive changes) This  condition can often be diagnosed based on your symptoms and the results of a blood test. It's important for vitamin B12 or folate deficiency anaemia to be diagnosed and treated as soon as possible. Although many of the symptoms improve with treatment, some problems caused by the condition can be irreversible if left untreated. The longer the condition goes untreated, the higher the chance of permanent damage. What blocks B12 absorption? Anti-intrinsic factor antibodies bind to and inhibit the effects of intrinsic factors, resulting in an inability of B12 to be absorbed by the terminal ileum. The body to produces abnormally large red blood cells that can't function properly. Treatment... To treat this condition you may be given Cyanocobalamin (B12) orally Although in my opinion and it's only my opinion having B12 the oral way may not be as effective as the body has to absorb it. An alternative treatment involves an injection of vitamin B12 once a month. People with severely low levels of B12 may need more shots in the beginning. Myself,  I have 3/6 monthly blood tests carried out, and my levels fluctuate. I will post an overview post that is slightly simpler with a diagram of the nervous system and nerve cells. I've included a picture that points to the food that is rich in B12 as it's important for all of us in our dietary requirements. As lacking B12 in your diet can make you B12 deficient. If your body is unable to absorb B12, then that's when you need to be looking more towards the monthly injections but of course by this stage you will be under your Dr's instructions as to what is best to be prescribed for your health needs. In my experience nerve pain can be absolutely excruciating, difficult to describe in words if you want my total honesty. Nerve pain can be the result of an injury, it can be a symptom of a chronic illness or even a lasting result after surgery. In my case it's the result of some 30+ surgeries and my chronic illness Fibromyalgia. I'm prescribed medication to help towards the severity of the pain, in no way does this eradicate the pain but it helps. One of my conditions is peripheral neurothopy. Here is some information on symptoms, causes and treatments. Sensory neuropathy – damage to the nerves that carry messages of touch, temperature, pain and other sensations to the brain. Symptoms of sensory neuropathy can include: ● Pins and needles in the affected body part ● Numbness and less ability to feel pain or changes in temperature, particularly in your feet ● A burning or sharp pain, usually in the feet ● Feeling pain from something that should not be painful at all, such as a very light touch ● Loss of balance or co-ordination caused by less ability to tell the position of the feet or hands. Some of the health conditions that can cause peripheral neurothopy >>> ● Low levels of vitamin B12 or other vitamins ● Physical damage to the nerves, such as from an injury or during surgery ● An underactive thyroid ● Shingles  The 4  above conditions are the cause of mine. Ways to be diagnosed ● Blood tests, especially to check for causes such as diabetes or vitamin B12 deficiency. Confirming if you have a neuropathy>>> Some people may need to see a neurologist, a specialist in health conditions affecting the nervous system, in hospital for further tests. These may include: ● A nerve conduction test (NCS), where small metal wires called electrodes are placed on your skin that release tiny electric shocks to stimulate your nerves; the speed and strength of the nerve signal is measured. ● Electromyography (EMG), where a small needle is inserted through your skin into your muscle and used to measure the electrical activity of your muscles NCS and EMG are usually carried out at the same time. Treating the underlying cause There are many different causes of peripheral neuropathy, some of which can be treated in different ways. But the underlying cause may not always be treatable. Relieving nerve pain... You may also require medicine to treat any nerve pain (neuropathic pain) you're experiencing Unlike most other types of pain, neuropathic pain does not usually get better with common painkillers, such as paracetamol and ibuprofen, and other medicines are often used. These should usually be started at the minimum dose with the dose gradually increased until you notice an effect. Higher doses may be better at managing the pain, but are also more likely to cause side effects. The most common side effects are..  tiredness, dizziness or feeling "drunk". If you get these, it may be necessary to reduce your dose. Many of these medicines may also be used for treating other health conditions, such as depression, epilepsy anxiety or headaches. If you're given an antidepressant, this may treat pain even if you're not depressed. This does not mean the doctor suspects you're depressed. Throughout my whole life, I’ve always been one to put others before myself. I’ve been there for people, no matter the cost to myself and despite the personal challenges I may have been facing at the time. It’s in my core, both personally and professionally. When my baby boy was born, our lives changed completely due to his medical complexities. And yet I still gave everyone else my all. Over the last 6 years, there have been times when I’ve needed others who quite simply, did not show up in the way I needed them to. And that was OK when Ruairi Bear was alive as I still had him to focus my all on. In the aftermath of his death, I’ve now realised that that was not OK. My heart has broken into a million pieces and I can no longer put others first. I can no longer listen to and support those who have not been there for me. I can no longer endure the pain to save them the hurt. I can no longer push aside my own feelings for the sake of others. I can no longer pretend that everything is OK. Because I am just as important as others and I need to look after me now. I owe my girls and my husband that. And I owe myself that. I really do wish that some of those I have needed in the past could have been able to see just how much I needed them. I wish they could have seen the cracks.
